neat wine noun

also undiluted wine, wine without water, straight wine

classical

Plaut. Curc. 128: ingurgitat impūra in sē merum avāriter
Hor. Ep. 1.19.11 (Lewis & Short)

merum, merī n.

noun, second declension

wine not mixed with water

The neuter of merus, pure, with vīnum understood. Wine was normally drunk with water; merum is the drinker’s word. Poetic and post-Augustan as a noun (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Hoc vidē ut ingurgitat impūra in sē merum avāriter, faucibus plēnīs.

    Just look how the filthy creature pours neat wine into herself, greedily, by the throatful.Plaut. Curc. 128

See also wine, honey wine, drunk, guzzle.
